evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is stored as a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-01-01"} returned 200 and the todo showed dueDate 2026-01-01. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and the todo showed dueDate null.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30" returned 400. POST with "01.02.2026" returned 400. PATCH with "2026-02-30" returned 400. PATCH with "abc" returned 400. Each response body was {"error":"dueDate must be a YYYY-MM-DD date or null"}.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC is 2026-11-01. I created these todos: past-due (2026-10-01), future-due (2026-12-01), due today (2026-11-01), no due date, and past-due but done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due, not-done todo. Todos that are due in the future or today, have no due date, or are done were excluded. The overdue flag was false for all of those. For the done todo it was true before PATCH {"done":true} and false after.
evidence.AC5: Loading / in the browser showed the list items "past (2026-10-01) überfällig", "future (2026-12-01)", "today (2026-11-01)", "nodue" and "pastdone ✓ (2026-10-01)". Each todo that has a due date shows it.
evidence.AC6: On the list page only the "past" todo, which was overdue, carried the word "überfällig". The future, today, no-due-date and done-but-past-due todos had no such label.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled "nur überfällige". After I clicked it, the list showed only the single item "past (2026-10-01) überfällig".
